feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the experience shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid platform/operations depth. It reads professionally, but impact would be stronger with more quantified outcomes, less repetition across skills sections, and a few wording/style fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, showing increasing leadership, ownership, and strategic responsibility.  
- Strong credibility through concrete platforms/tools and scale indicators (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers).  
- Writing is polished and audience-appropriate, with a strong executive summary and consistent mission-driven positioning.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond scope metrics: e.g., growth in engagement, email performance, efficiency gains, cost savings, adoption rates, or campaign results.  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidate to improve structure and save space.  
- Minor language/style edits: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “more than 12 years of experience”; keep punctuation around lists more consistent (some bullets use serial commas, some do not); “A2/Learning” is stylistically awkward—use “French (A2, currently learning)” instead. No major misspellings or obvious typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear positioning, but it’s slightly generic and overlaps heavily with Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and foregrounding recent leadership in digital transformation will make it sharper.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and grammar.
- Lead with your current value proposition: digital strategy, platform modernization, and communications leadership for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Replace broad lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) with a more concise framing like “multi-channel digital communications.”
- Consider rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience driving multi-channel communications, platform modernization, and editorial operations for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in digital transformation, cross-functional stakeholder coordination, and building scalable workflows and systems. Strong background in advocacy and policy communications, translating complex issues into clear, accessible content and user-focused digital experiences.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows and systems” repeat Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Advocacy messaging” and stakeholder coordination are also reinforced in Work Experience and Topline Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, senior-level language: “Digital transformation strategy” instead of “Digital strategy & transformation,” “Cross-functional stakeholder leadership” instead of “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination.”
- Align wording with the strongest recent experience: “CMS modernization & web operations,” “Editorial governance & workflow design,” “Analytics, reporting & performance optimization.”
- Standardize style and parallel structure; use either all noun phrases or all “X & Y” constructions.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital transformation strategy • Cross-channel communications leadership • CMS modernization & web operations • Editorial governance & workflow design • Analytics, reporting & performance optimization • Content systems architecture • Cross-functional stakeholder leadership • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia production & live event delivery

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communication” duplicates the header and Topline Skills.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Soft Skills; keep this block focused on strategic/professional capabilities.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with the projects footer and prior NACo leadership bullets. Tighten around outcomes, scale, and what is new at this engagement.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper lead: “Embedded strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvement, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise”) with ownership verbs: “Built,” “Led,” “Designed,” “Implemented,” “Established.”
- Consolidate into 4–5 bullets focused on impact, e.g. Drupal campaign builds, enterprise workflows/analytics, cross-channel governance, AI search initiative, and front-end/CMS delivery.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages/users, publishing teams supported, toolkit downloads, workflow time saved, search accuracy/engagement gains, campaign launch volume.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search initiative” and Drupal microsite work duplicate the Recent Projects section; keep this item at the leadership/outcomes level and let the footer hold examples.
- Governance, analytics, and enterprise web improvement also echo the 2022–2024 NACo role; emphasize consulting/embedded delivery and new technical execution.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It would be sharper if the opening emphasized enterprise ownership and if channel-management bullets added clearer outcomes rather than broad scope.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opener with: “Directed enterprise digital communications strategy, platforms, analytics, governance, and budget for NACo’s web, email, social, and video ecosystem.”
- Tighten and front-load impact: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-based: add metrics for email performance, audience growth, engagement, production volume, or cost/time savings if available.
- Combine operations/analytics bullets for concision: “Built reporting infrastructure across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery while formalizing governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the prior NACo role; in this entry, stress enterprise leadership, platform modernization, analytics, and governance.
- Video studio/buildout may overlap with footer projects; keep this bullet focused on organizational capability created.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with both the earlier NACo role and the later Director role. Make it more clearly about operating ownership, editorial coordination, and channel growth at the manager-to-director transition point.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead line to emphasize scope and progression: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-focused: “Launched and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring channel for policy communications.”
- Clarify operational impact: “Improved cross-team editorial planning and digital publishing workflows, increasing consistency and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Helping scale” and “helped improve” sound soft; use direct ownership language.
- Avoid repeating website, analytics, governance, or studio-building themes already covered more strongly in the Director role.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo/consulting bullets. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and distinctive strengths rather than repeating generic communications phrases.

Suggested edit
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive bullets:
- Enterprise digital strategy for public-sector organizations
- Editorial governance and content operations at scale
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social and video
- Audience-centered campaign and information architecture planning
- Drop “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” unless targeting explicitly advocacy-heavy roles; it’s already well covered elsewhere.
- Prefer “content operations at scale” over “content planning” to better reflect recent leadership in governance, workflows, and publisher systems.
- If space allows, add scale language tied to recent work, e.g., “for 10,000+ page platforms” or “supporting 50+ publishers.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” duplicate both the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” is also repeated in Core Competencies and multiple recent roles.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool dump and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and current strengths, not every individual technology.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as a tighter, impact-oriented line: Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search experiences
- Remove lower-priority or older/platform-specific items unless central to target roles: WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, jQuery.
- Group skills by capability, not product list; “front-end implementation” is stronger than listing basic languages.
- If you want one proof point, tie to recent work in adjacent sections rather than here, e.g., Drupal modernization or AI search.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills broader and reserve full tool inventory for Technical + IT.
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already echo Core Competencies, so avoid repeating the same phrasing elsewhere verbatim.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools for a senior digital leader, but this item is too list-like and overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT.” In Topline Skills, emphasize strategic application and decision-making rather than repeating software names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool inventory to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Analytics strategy, KPI design & executive reporting.”
- Group tools more tightly: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity” instead of separate bullets.
- Replace “SEO and performance analysis” with broader, higher-value language such as “search, content and user-behavior optimization.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy & KPI design • Executive and leadership reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI & Microsoft Clarity • Search, content and user-behavior optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Core Competencies” (“Analytics and reporting infrastructure”) and “Technical + IT” (“Data, Analytics & Optimization”); keep Topline Skills more strategic, Technical + IT more tool-specific.
- Avoid repeating exact tool lists elsewhere unless this is the only analytics-focused skills section.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo bullets. Make it more senior, operational, and distinct from the broader “multimedia production and livestream operations” language already elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Broadcast & Event Production” to sound more leadership-level and concise.
- Replace generic bullets with sharper terms: “Broadcast video production,” “Livestream and webcast production,” “PTZ camera and control-room workflows,” “Studio buildout and operations,” “Hybrid event technical delivery.”
- If accurate, add scale or ownership language: “in-house studio operations” or “broadcast-quality event production.”
- Keep to 4–5 bullets max and avoid repeating tools already listed under Technical + IT.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” and “Hybrid and virtual event production” overlap with Core Competencies’ “multimedia production and livestream operations.”
- “Video production and editing” is partly duplicated by “Premiere Pro” and “Podcast production” in Technical + IT; keep this section focused on capabilities, not tools.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should either add proficiency/context or be trimmed to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- If space allows, prioritize by strength/relevance: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- Consider adding level/scope only where defensible, e.g., “Drupal (10,000+ page migration; custom microsites)” to connect directly to recent impact.
- Keep this item platform-only; leave modernization, APIs, and AI search to other technical sections.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” Topline Skills entry almost exactly; consider removing one or making this version more specific.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel lightweight versus enterprise platforms unless it supports a notable project.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, analytics, automation, and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End Development & Technical Implementation
- Replace with a tighter list: HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers unless required by the role; “HTML/CSS” is cleaner than “HTML5 • CSS3.”
- If space allows, add one outcome-oriented qualifier in a summary elsewhere, e.g., “used for CMS customization, analytics deployment, and workflow automation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills; consider removing them from one section.
- “GitHub Actions” and “Cloudflare Workers” are useful differentiators here, so keep those over more generic items.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation”/“Airtable systems” already called out elsewhere. Tighten it to emphasize automation/platform-building tools over general collaboration apps.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to highlight systems capability: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira/Asana • Slack/Teams integrations”
- Remove lower-value generic PM/chat tools unless central to target roles; keep the strongest, most relevant platforms only.
- If space allows, add a qualifier for impact: “workflow automation, intake/tracking systems, cross-team approvals, notifications”
- Consider renaming the category to “Workflow Automation & Operations Systems” for stronger alignment with recent consulting and director-level work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same idea verbatim.
- Jira, Asana, Basecamp, Trello, Slack, and Teams are broad collaboration tools; listing all may dilute stronger technical signals.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools for this profile, but the line is too bare and undersells email-platform depth shown in recent NACo roles. Make it more specific and aligned to campaign operations, segmentation, and member communications.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms
- Rewrite as: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, strengthen with functional context: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (campaign automation, segmentation) • Higher Logic (member email/community engagement) • Mailchimp (newsletter operations)
- Keep only platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; order by strongest/recentest platform rather than alphabetically.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This item overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies and multiple NACo bullets about newsletters/email; avoid adding generic phrases like “email marketing” without tool-specific detail.
- If Dynamics 365 was not used in a recent role, consider dropping it to keep the technical section tightly matched to recent experience.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to early-team building, web refresh support, and multimedia production.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and contribution, not generic support: “Promoted across two digital roles as part of NACo’s first in-house digital team, helping formalize workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add clearer action/result language: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, to expand the organization’s in-house communications capacity.”
- Tighten the management point: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate on daily production and publishing.”
- If available, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, publishing volume, or efficiency gains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/producing the format, not expanding it.
- Avoid repeating workflow/governance language already used more strongly in the 2022–2024 role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia/digital trajectory, but it reads generic and underplays impact. Tighten it to emphasize cross-functional coordination and the “first podcast” milestone.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground scope and initiative: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the digital work more active and specific: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support organizational communications and member engagement.”
- Keep the standout achievement concise: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, production and rollout.”
- If possible, add one measurable outcome: number of episodes, audience growth, internal stakeholders supported, or projects delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad “digital content production” language used in later NACo roles; this entry should lean more on innovation/research support and the podcast launch.
- Don’t overemphasize video/multimedia here if those become stronger, more senior achievements in later roles.
